title.en: Leading Analytical Work: Review, Standards and Stakeholders
title.ar: قيادة العمل التحليلي: المراجعة والمعايير وأصحاب المصلحة

tagline: Set the unit's quality standard, run review as a system, and hold the line on evidence with sponsors
description: Participants lead the analytics unit of the fictional Ras Sahil Ports Authority: twelve analysts whose work increasingly starts as an assistant's draft. They write a proportionate quality-assurance standard and review checklist, re-run and review colleagues' analyses, set the unit's rules for AI-assisted work, turn review findings into feedback, and negotiate scope, deadline and evidence with role-played sponsors, one of whom asks for an unfavourable result to be dropped. DS-310 teaches reviewing one analysis; this course sets the standards and runs the system.
audience: Specialists. Data scientists who have completed the level 300 core and practicum, or can show equivalent work: an analysis they led from question to recommendation and defended.
prerequisites: DS-310 Problem Framing and Analytical Review
Has reviewed an analysis written by someone else and written comments the author acted on
Uses version control for analysis code

Setup: a laptop processor with uv, or Google Colab. Nothing downloads a model; a free hosted model key is optional (every assistant and tutor cell has a stand-in). Run 00_setup_check before Day 1; see labs/README.md.

outcomes.text: Design a proportionate quality-assurance standard for analytical work, with assurance levels, a review checklist and sign-off rules, given the unit's log of 30 requests with their uses and risks
outcomes.evidence: a standard with which a peer, working independently, assigns the same assurance levels to six new requests

outcomes.text: Review analyses by others, including assistant-drafted ones, rank findings by their effect on the decision and calibrate severity with a second reviewer, given three seeded-flaw analysis repositories
outcomes.evidence: review notes that find the seeded critical flaws, and a severity agreement table with the second reviewer

outcomes.text: Design rules for AI-assisted analysis covering verification, disclosure and the process evidence each analyst keeps, and audit the unit's work against them, given the national generative AI guidelines and a log of the unit's assisted analyses
outcomes.evidence: a one-page rule set and an audit of five assisted analyses against it

outcomes.text: Prepare feedback and a development plan for an analyst from review findings, given a reviewed notebook and the analyst's skills profile
outcomes.evidence: a feedback note and three-month plan that a peer judges specific

outcomes.text: Lead a negotiation with a sponsor on scope, deadline and evidence threshold and record the agreement, given a role-played sponsor whose constraints change during the meeting
outcomes.evidence: an analysis agreement and an observer's rubric score

outcomes.text: Decide how to respond to pressure to change or suppress a finding, and record the reasons, given a scripted request to remove an unfavourable subgroup result
outcomes.evidence: a decision record citing the unit's standard and the ethics principles

case_study.name: Ras Sahil Ports Authority
case_study.summary: Ras Sahil Ports Authority is a fictional Gulf-coast port authority whose analytics unit of twelve analysts serves marine operations, commercial affairs, finance and staffing, with more and more work starting as a draft by Musawwada, the unit's drafting assistant. Participants, as the unit's head, write the assurance standard from a log of 30 requests, adapt a published checklist, re-run a colleague's cargo-dwell repository, set rules for assisted work and audit five assisted analyses, calibrate severity with a second reviewer on a seeded-flaw berth-delay analysis, write feedback and a review rota, and negotiate scope, evidence and a pressured subgroup finding with two role-played sponsors. The capstone is the quality-assurance pack for the marine pilot staffing analysis. All data is synthetic and generated with a fixed seed.

format_note: Intensive: 3 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task

days.title: Set the standard

sessions.title: Assurance proportionate to risk
sessions.summary: Four roles, business risk as effect and likelihood, and four assurance levels a peer can apply
outcomes: Explain the four assurance roles and why the assurer is independent of the analyst
Grade a request by the effect of an error and the complexity of the work
Assign an assurance level with a matrix a peer applies the same way

lab.title: Six requests, four levels
lab.summary: Read the unit's log of 30 requests, write the assurance matrix with its escalators, grade six new requests by risk and complexity, and compare your levels with a second reviewer's.

steps.text: Read the log: where errors after release came from
Write the matrix and its escalators
Grade the six new requests
Compare with the second reviewer and tighten one definition

lab.stretch: Add the sign-off rules: who may approve at each level

sessions.title: A team review checklist
sessions.summary: From a personal checklist to the unit's: adapt a published one, item by item, and tie each item to a level
outcomes: Adapt a published checklist to the unit's work instead of adopting it whole
Write each item as a question answered with evidence
Tie each item to the assurance levels, with a privacy and classification check in every level

lab.title: A checklist adapted from REFORMS
lab.summary: Draft a checklist from question to conclusion by adapting a published reproducibility checklist (REFORMS, 32 items): keep, rewrite or drop each item, add the privacy and classification check, and set the level at which each item applies.

steps.text: Map the 32 items to the five review areas
Keep, rewrite or drop each item
Add the privacy and classification item
Set the level of each item and test the length

lab.stretch: Add one item for work an assistant drafted

sessions.title: Reproducibility as a team rule
sessions.summary: Re-run before reading: the failures a re-run finds and the repository rules that prevent them
outcomes: Re-run an analysis from its repository before reading its conclusions
Classify reproduction failures by kind
Write repository rules that make a re-run routine

lab.title: Re-run Saleh's repository
lab.summary: Re-run a colleague's cargo-dwell analysis from its repository, record every step that failed and its kind, and reproduce the reported figure.

steps.text: Follow the README exactly
Log each failure with its kind
Fix a copy until it runs
Reproduce the reported figure or explain the gap

lab.stretch: Write the repository rule that would have prevented each failure

sessions.title: Rules for AI-assisted analysis
sessions.summary: What an analyst verifies, discloses and keeps when an assistant drafts the work
outcomes: Turn the national generative AI guidelines into rules for analytical work
Specify the process evidence each analyst keeps
Test a rule set on real cases before adopting it

lab.title: Rules for assisted work
lab.summary: Write what analysts must verify, disclose and keep as evidence when an assistant drafts work, on one page, and test the rules on eight scenarios from the unit.

steps.text: Read the guideline duties
Write the verify, disclose and keep rules
Decide eight scenarios with your rules
Cut the rules to one page

lab.stretch: Add the unaided-practice rule: work each analyst still does without the assistant

days.subtitle: An assurance standard, a team checklist, re-runs as a rule and rules for assisted work

days.title: Review and develop

sessions.title: Calibrating reviewers
sessions.summary: Severity by effect on the decision, rated alone, then compared and turned into clearer wording
outcomes: Rate review findings by their effect on the decision
Measure agreement between two reviewers, beyond chance
Turn disagreements into clearer checklist wording

lab.title: Two reviewers, one analysis
lab.summary: Review a seeded-flaw berth-delay analysis independently with a partner (AI-off), compare severity ratings in an agreement table, and revise the checklist where you disagree.

steps.text: Re-run and review alone
Rate each finding by its effect on the decision
Agreement table and weighted kappa
Revise the checklist where you disagreed

lab.stretch: Measure what each flaw does to the headline by fixing it alone

sessions.title: Auditing assisted work
sessions.summary: An audit checks the evidence a rule asks for, recomputes what it can and records each breach with its rule
outcomes: Audit work against rules from its evidence, not its claims
Recompute a number an assistant drafted
Record each breach with the rule it breaks

lab.title: Audit five assisted analyses
lab.summary: Check five assistant-drafted analyses from the unit's log against the rules for AI-assisted work, recompute the one headline that can be recomputed, and record each breach with its rule.

steps.text: Read the rules and the log
Check each record against the rules
Recompute one headline number
Write the audit table

lab.stretch: Propose the one rule change the audit suggests

sessions.title: Feedback that builds skill
sessions.summary: From findings to feedback that names the reasoning, and a plan that keeps unaided practice in the work
outcomes: Choose the findings worth raising with an analyst
Write feedback that names the reasoning, not only the error
Plan development with goals, evidence and unaided practice

lab.title: Feedback and a three-month plan
lab.summary: Turn review findings on a new analyst's notebook into a feedback note that names the reasoning, and a three-month plan built on her skills profile.

steps.text: Choose three findings to raise
Write each note: observation, effect, reasoning, next step
A three-month plan from the skills profile
Check that every line is specific

lab.stretch: Write the two-line summary for the analyst's file

sessions.title: Review capacity and mentoring
sessions.summary: Review hours follow assurance levels; senior reviewers are the bottleneck; pairings develop analysts
outcomes: Estimate a quarter's review hours from assurance levels
Assign reviewers under separation and seniority rules
Use review pairings to develop analysts

lab.title: A quarter's review rota
lab.summary: Plan a quarter's review load and pairings for a team of twelve: assign 40 planned analyses to reviewers under the separation and seniority rules, find the shortfall and choose how to close it.

steps.text: Review hours by level for the quarter
Assign reviewers under the rules
Find the overload and the shortfall
Pair the juniors with mentors

lab.stretch: Choose which mid-level analyst trains as a level 3 reviewer, and how

days.title: Work with sponsors

sessions.title: Scope and deadline

steps.text: Size the questions against the deadline
Open the meeting and ask
Respond when the constraints change
Record the scope agreement
The observer's score

sessions.summary: The decision rule and an evidence threshold the data can detect, written and signed before the analysis
outcomes: Write the decision rule before the analysis
Check an evidence threshold against what the data can detect
Record roles and sign-off in the agreement

lab.summary: Write an analysis agreement for the pilot decision: question, decision rule and an evidence threshold the data can detect, with roles and sign-off.

steps.text: The decision and its options
Compute the change the data can detect
Set the decision rule and the threshold
Roles, level and sign-off

lab.stretch: Say in the agreement what happens when the result falls between the thresholds

sessions.title: Pressure on a finding
sessions.summary: Challenge or pressure: check the finding, weigh the options, decide and record the reasons

Respond with options that keep the finding

lab.title: Drop the feeder result?
lab.summary: Handle a scripted request to drop an unfavourable subgroup (feeder vessels) from the pilot evaluation: recompute it, weigh the options, decide, and record the decision citing the unit's standard and the ethics principles.

steps.text: Read the request and recompute the subgroup
Weigh the options
Decide and write the decision record
Draft the reply

sessions.title: Reporting quality and correcting errors
sessions.summary: A quality statement says what was checked, by whom and what is uncertain; a correction says what changed, fast
outcomes: Write a quality statement a board can read

lab.title: A quality statement and a correction
lab.summary: Draft a board-paper quality statement for the pilot evaluation (what was checked, by whom, what remains uncertain) and a correction notice for the Q2 cargo-dwell figure found wrong after release.

steps.text: Write the quality statement
Find and size the Q2 error
Write the correction notice
Check both against the standard

lab.stretch: Decide who is told of the correction, and in which order
